The chart above illustrates how often students in a university take part in volunteer activities each month. According to the survey, 35 percent of the students never participate in volunteer work, while 45 percent volunteer one or two times a month, and only 20 percent do so three times or more.

Two factors may explain this pattern. On the one hand, many students are under heavy academic pressure, so they give priority to their studies and regard volunteer work as a luxury. On the other hand, some students are willing to help others, but they lack information about how to join suitable programs.

In my view, volunteer activities deserve more attention. Through volunteering, students can gain practical skills, broaden their horizons and develop a stronger sense of responsibility. Therefore, the university should provide more opportunities and timely information, and students should learn to balance study with service to society.
